newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ says "B" share increase helps unlock value.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ says "B" share increase helps unlock value.

text.p: Air New Zealand Ltd said on Monday the increase in the proportion of "B" shares on issue would help unlock the capital value of the company as a whole.

As part of its purchase of 50 percent of Ansett Holdings from TNT Ltd for a total of NZ$540 million, Air New Zealand has won approval from the New Zealand government to lift the proportion of "B" shares, which can be held by foreign investors, from 35 percent to 49 percent,

The company will make a three for 11 renounceable rights issue to raise NZ$240 million to fund the acquisition. Holders of the "A" shares, which are limited to New Zealand residents, will be able to reclassify their entitlements as "B" shares.

The directors said they had been aware for some time of an imbalance in demand for the two types of shares and the lack of liquidity in the "B" shares had constrained the market prices of both securities.
Increasing the proportion of "B" shares "is an important step in unlocking the capital value the market attributes to the company as a whole," the directors said in a statement.

They said allowing all shareholders to participate in a pro rata rights issue at a common price for the "A" and "B" shares was considered to be the most fair and equitable method of achieving this outcome.
